title: MCP Resources and Prompts: Addressable Context for Stateless Servers
service: uricatalog: an MCP 2026-07-28 notes catalog (resources, prompts, subscriptions/listen) with a host-side dbm response cache, a shared-channel client and a resource-template router

parts.lesson_anchor: Resources Are Stable URI Contracts (-32602 with data.uri); Prompts Are User-Controlled Templates (a prompt is no side channel around resource access); Subscriptions (accepted subset, subscription ID on every event); code/main.py resources_read, prompts_get, subscriptions_listen, SubscriptionStream
planted_bugs: handle_prompts_get looks the note up in the catalog itself and only checks that it exists, so bob gets alice's private note through review_note

readable_contents returns an empty list for an unknown or unreadable URI, so resources/read answers with empty contents; after routing the prompt through it, the failure surfaces one call up as an IndexError on contents[0]
accept_filter keeps every truthy field of the request, so unknown fields, "promptsListChanged": "yes" and a flag of 1 reach the acknowledgment (value == True still lets 1 and 1.0 through)
SubscriptionHub.resource_updated scans every stream's URI list on every update, O(streams x URIs)
parts.timing_assert: 100 streams x 3000 URIs, 1200 updates under 0.1 s after gc.collect(): the scan takes 1.1 to 2.2 s, the URI index about 1 ms (at most 1.5 ms in 15 runs)
parts.overfix_guard: the index delivers notes://note-1 only to exact subscribers (not notes://note-10), keeps two clients that both listen with id 17 apart, builds each event with its own stream's id, stops delivering after close(), sends list_changed only to streams that accepted it (including a stream with no URIs), and accept_filter still answers a malformed filter with -32602
parts.deviation: review_note embeds the note's text (the lesson's prompt only names the URI), so the missing authorization leaks content instead of only existence. The timing uses 100 streams x 3000 URIs and 1200 updates instead of 2000 x 2000: a 4-million-entry index takes about 2 s to build, and this size already makes the scan 1.1 to 2.2 s. The accepted subset is protocol-level (fields, exact true, deduplicated sorted URIs), as suggested; filtering out URIs the caller cannot read is a follow-up question.

parts.deviation: The cursor records the last URI and the caller, not a catalog version. Keyset paging by URI already stays correct when notes are added or removed between pages, so a version check would either do nothing or force every listing to restart after any change. Lesson 28 lists binding to a catalog version as one choice a server may make.

parts.lesson_anchor: Subscriptions Use a Client-Opened Response Stream: acknowledgment before any event, the event carries no document so the client reads again, a graceful end is a complete response to the original listen request, several subscriptions share one stdio channel and the subscription ID demultiplexes them
parts.wire_format: NDJSON action log, one record per action, decided by the test's endswith, splitlines and json.loads per line
